_why_this_file_exists: MP.B1 was directed on 2026-08-13 with none of these open, from series structure alone. It invented its opening, moved the scene to the wrong room, described the hero prop's defining sound backwards and put invented words in Richard's mouth. Julian caught it in one question: 'surely we need the beginning of this story for Tom Chen to come into the shop with it and tell the story — have you followed the script exactly.' No beat is directed again before the script for it is open.

hero_prop_law.the_sound: A French tune, sweet and WRONG. 'The same notes bent the same way, every time.' The manuscript is emphatic: 'Not broken wrong. Not clunk and jangle wrong.'
hero_prop_law.why_it_is_law: A box that sounds broken can simply be fixed, and the episode has no mystery. A box that is crooked ON PURPOSE is the entire plot, the reveal, and the ending. MP.B1 described it as 'three halting notes, the third one sour' — backwards.
hero_prop_law.the_worn_place: A small worn place on the lid where a thumb has rested for a hundred years. It is the episode's rhyme: Rose sees it in Act One, Pascal's thumb rests on the same spot in 1867, Richard polishes it in Act Three, Tom touches it at the end. Every plate of the box must carry it.

the_apron_ritual: Over the head, tied at the back, both hands smoothing the front — then, and only then, he lifts the box. Then he goes very still. Manuscript: 'like a knight settling his armour.' Its first appearance sets it for the series.
arc_seeds_in_the_tag: The gold paint tin never gets emptier. Albert checked twice and drew lines.
Everything the door gives them is wrong — except their shoes. Script broadens the manuscript's 'Peggi's clogs' to 'why do OUR shoes fit?'
A small wooden box on Richard's high shelf, behind the solvent jars. He looked at it for half a second before turning out the light.
Richard's closing line about his wife's clock — 'Your grandmother's clock says quarter past. It's half three. I'll have a look at THAT next.'
